candidates.change_summary: Change the return value from true to false.
Replace the require(_tos.length > 0) precondition with require(_tos.length == 0), so the function returns true instead of reverting when called with an empty _tos array.
Change the transferFrom selector string to transfer(address,uint256), causing a different external call to be made.
Move the transferFrom selector string into a different namespace (transferFrom(address,address,uint256) to transferFrom(address,address,uint)), changing the requested selector.
Change the loop condition from i < _tos.length to i <= _tos.length, causing one extra out-of-bounds access that usually reverts.
Change the loop index initialization from i = 0 to i = 1, skipping the first transfer.
Change the per-iteration increment from i++ to ++i, altering when the index is advanced relative to the external call.
Swap the from and _tos[i] arguments in the external call, changing the transferFrom source and destination.
Change the value argument of the external call from v to 0, causing zero-value transfers to be attempted.
Invert the external call success check to if (_s) so it reverts on success and continues on failure.
Change the successful return value from true to false.
Change the require guard from `_tos.length > 0` to `_tos.length == 0`, so the function only proceeds for empty arrays and otherwise reverts.
Replace the selector hash string with a different function signature, causing the encoded call data to select a different callee function.
Initialize the loop counter to 1 instead of 0, skipping the first element of _tos.
Change the loop condition to use `<=` instead of `<`, causing an out-of-bounds access and revert on non-empty input.
Increment the loop counter by 2 instead of 1, processing only every other element of _tos.
Replace `_tos[i]` with `_tos[0]` in the calldata, so every call transfers to the first destination instead of each loop destination.
Replace the per-destination value `v` with `0` in the calldata, making every underlying call a zero-value transfer.
Invert the call-success check to `if (_s)`, causing a revert exactly when the external call succeeds.
Remove the revert on a failed external call, so unsuccessful underlying calls no longer abort transfer.
Return false instead of true on the successful completion path.
Change the require condition to always revert by requiring false.
Replace the hardcoded return value true with false.
Delete the entire require statement so that empty _tos array does not revert.
Replace the for-loop condition `i < _tos.length` with `i <= _tos.length`, causing one extra out-of-bounds iteration.
Delete the return statement so the function returns the default false instead of true.
Delete the require that _tos has at least one element, so an empty _tos array no longer reverts and the function returns true.
Replace the loop condition i < _tos.length with i <= _tos.length, causing one extra iteration when _tos is non-empty (out-of-bounds access or extra call).
Replace the selector with keccak256("transfer(address,uint256)"), changing the called function on caddress so calls may revert differently.
Replace the low-level call target caddress with from, sending the call to the wrong address and changing revert behavior.
Replace the revert() in the failed-call branch with a no-op, so failed calls no longer cause the function to revert.
Replace return true with return false, flipping the successful return value observed by callers.
